html:
The Falepili Union is a treaty between Australia and Tuvalu, signed in November 2023 and in force from 2024. It lets up to 280 Tuvaluans a year move to Australia to live, work and study, as the rising sea threatens their islands.

Tuvalu is a group of low coral atolls in the Pacific, home to about 11,000 people. Most of its land is only a few metres above the sea, and rising seas caused by climate change already flood homes and spoil wells with salt water. The treaty was the first to offer a whole nation a path to move because of climate change.

Falepili is a Tuvaluan word for good neighbourliness. In return for the migration pathway and a promise of help after disasters and attacks, Tuvalu agreed to consult Australia before making security deals with any other country. Critics in Tuvalu said this gave away too much; others saw it as Australia pushing back against China's growing reach in the Pacific. The deal was signed by Anthony Albanese and Tuvalu's prime minister Kausea Natano.
